subject: Temporary retention exception for analytics logs — proposed controls
messages:
From: Asha Menon <asha@finlytics.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: CloudGuard Legal <legal@cloudguard.io>, FinLytics Security <security@finlytics.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary exception for ephemeral logs used in analytics pipeline

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this. We're close to go-live on the analytics feature but one technical constraint from our side requires Redwood to retain a narrow set of ephemeral request logs for a short period to reconcile billing and attribution across EU hosts. Specifically: a) request-level metadata (timestamp, request id, model id, region tag) and b) a trimmed response hash (not full content).

Our security team is asking for a documented exception in the DPA for a temporary retention up to 30 days, limited to EU data centers, with:
- encryption at rest and in transit;
- role-based admin access and MFA logging;
- documented proof-of-erasure on demand;
- explicit export control language preventing cross-border transfer without prior approval.

Attached a small diagram of the data flow and a short high-level compliance checklist. Can you confirm what is feasible from Redwood's operational controls and suggest redline language we can propose?

Also flag if there is any impact on your standard erase certification timelines — our auditors are pretty strict about confirmation within 72 hours of request.

Appreciate a quick read — we hope to finalize before the end of next week.

Best,
Asha Menon
Head of Product, FinLytics
asha@finlytics.com
Attachment: pipeline-diagram.pdf (diagram, 120Kb)
From: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha@finlytics.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Mar 2028 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary exception for ephemeral logs used in analytics pipeline

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear note and diagram. Circling back with operational constraints and a suggested approach. Summary answer up front: we can support a bounded exception for trimmed telemetry (metadata + response hash) with stricter controls, but we can't keep user or prompt content beyond short windows.

Operational controls we can commit to:
- Storage: encrypted at rest (AES-256) in our EU region (Frankfurt / Amsterdam) with customer region pinning;
- Access: role-based admin privileges, access audit trails retained for 12 months;
- Retention: propose a 14-day window as a default for telemetry; we can consider 21 days for agreed use-cases with documented justification;
- Proof-of-erasure: we can provide a Certificate of Deletion (CSV export listing erased object IDs + timestamp) within 5 business days of a valid request;
- Export controls: we will not egress the retained telemetry outside the EU region without explicit, signed approval from FinLytics.

Suggested DPA redline (proposal):
"Temporary Analytics Retention: For the limited purpose of billing reconciliation and operational analytics, Redwood may retain non-content telemetry (defined as request timestamps, request IDs, model identifiers, region tags, and cryptographic response hashes) for a maximum period of 14 days by default. Upon mutual written agreement this maximum may be extended to 21 days for specific workloads. Such retained telemetry shall be stored only in Customer-designated EU data centers, encrypted at rest and in transit, and accessible only to authorized Redwood personnel. Upon Customer request Redwood will provide a Certificate of Deletion describing objects removed and deletion timestamps within five (5) business days. Redwood shall not transfer retained telemetry outside the EU without prior written consent from the Customer."

Notes / constraints:
- We cannot provide raw response content as part of this exception; only hashes/metadata are possible.
- We can accelerate deletion evidence in higher-tier contracts (SLA-backed) if you need faster turnaround.

If this looks close to what you need, I suggest a short call tomorrow to walk through the redline and confirm the 14 vs 21 day window. I'll loop in Neha for legal wording and Marissa for product-to-product operational follow-ups.

Cheers,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Manager, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
From: Asha Menon <asha@finlytics.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: CloudGuard Legal <legal@cloudguard.io>, FinLytics Security <security@finlytics.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 08:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: temporary exception for ephemeral logs used in analytics pipeline

Thanks Olga — that is very helpful. We reviewed the proposed redline with CloudGuard Legal and FinLytics Security. Two quick counteritems:

1) Retention window: we can accept 21 days for this initial rollout (not 30).
2) Certificate of Deletion timeline: auditors want evidence within 72 hours where practicable. If you cannot guarantee 72 hours contractually, we need a path to an SLA-backed shortcut.

Proposed counter-redline (inline):
"Temporary Analytics Retention: For the limited purpose of billing reconciliation and operational analytics, Redwood may retain non-content telemetry (defined as request timestamps, request IDs, model identifiers, region tags, and cryptographic response hashes) for a maximum period of 21 days for agreed workloads. Such retained telemetry shall be stored only in Customer-designated EU data centers, encrypted at rest and in transit, and accessible only to authorized Redwood personnel with MFA. Upon Customer request Redwood will provide a Certificate of Deletion describing objects removed and deletion timestamps within seventy-two (72) hours for standard accounts and within forty-eight (48) hours where an SLA-backed deletion assurance is in place. Redwood shall not transfer retained telemetry outside the EU without prior written consent from the Customer."

Forwarded for visibility: CloudGuard Legal (legal@cloudguard.io) — please confirm if 72 hours is operationally feasible or if you require the 48-hour SLA path for enterprise customers only.

Attachment: compliance-checklist.xlsx (22Kb)

Asha
Head of Product, FinLytics
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha@finlytics.com>, CloudGuard Legal <legal@cloudguard.io>
Cc: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary exception for ephemeral logs used in analytics pipeline

Hi Asha / CloudGuard Legal — looping in a final operational + contract compromise that aligns with our internal SLAs. We appreciate the flexibility on the 21-day window; Redwood can accept the 21-day maximum for agreed workloads and will provide deletion evidence as follows:

- Standard deletion certification: Certificate of Deletion (CSV) within five (5) business days;
- Expedited deletion certification (72 hours): available for customers with a documented compliance need and executed amendment;
- SLA-backed expedited deletion (48 hours): available as a paid add-on (enterprise SLA) with commit and monitoring;

Revised contractual language we can commit to (final):
"Temporary Analytics Retention: For the limited purpose of billing reconciliation and operational analytics, Redwood may retain non-content telemetry (defined as request timestamps, request IDs, model identifiers, region tags, and cryptographic response hashes) for a maximum period of twenty-one (21) days for workloads mutually agreed in writing. Such retained telemetry shall be stored only in Customer-designated EU data centers, encrypted at rest and in transit, and accessible only to authorized Redwood personnel with multifactor authentication. Upon Customer request Redwood will provide a Certificate of Deletion describing objects removed and deletion timestamps within five (5) business days. For Customers that require expedited confirmation, Redwood offers a compliance amendment enabling a seventy-two (72) hour Certificate of Deletion for standard contracted customers, and a forty-eight (48) hour SLA-backed Certificate of Deletion as an enterprise add-on. Redwood shall not transfer retained telemetry outside the EU without prior written consent from the Customer."

Operational notes:
- We will add additional audit logging for admin access and mark the telemetry sets as subject to the customer's retention carveout in our system.
- Export controls: we'll add explicit contractual language to block any automated cross-border replication as part of the DPA.

Next steps: I can draft an amendment for your legal team and share via the DocuSign link (see thread metadata) for signature. Can we target final sign-off by EOD Friday?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
